\begin{example} \end{example}[Metric on a surface of revolution]

Source: petersen:page-0035 ↗ def:pet-ch1-frame-metric

1. ch1:1.4.4Let $c(t)=(r(t),0,z(t))$, with $r(t)>0$, and revolve it about the $z$-axis: \[ f(t,\theta )=(r(t)\cos \theta ,r(t)\sin \theta ,z(t)). \] The induced metric is \[ g=(\dot r^2+\dot z^2)dt^2+r^2d\theta ^2. \] When $c$ has unit speed, this becomes $dt^2+r^2d\theta ^2$. \end{example}
Proof

↗ ex:pet-ch1-surface-of-revolution

\sketch Substitution into $dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$ gives

\[ \begin{aligned} dx& =\dot r\cos \theta \, dt-r\sin \theta \, d\theta ,\\ dy& =\dot r\sin \theta \, dt+r\cos \theta \, d\theta ,\\ dz& =\dot z\, dt. \end{aligned} \]

The mixed terms cancel, leaving the displayed metric.
